comments.text: Found while testing reminder emails: INV-2026-0017 says 2.01 but its two lines add up to 2.02.
Bluefen Bakery paid 2.02 and asked why they "overpaid". Raising the priority.
Reproduced locally. Each line is 3 × 0.335 = 1.005, which rounds to 1.01. The total rounds the raw sum 2.010 to 2.01.
Only invoices with two or more lines ending in exactly half a cent. In the seed data that is only INV-2026-0017.
No data fix needed in the database: totals are computed, not stored.
Round per line or round the sum? Finance says: the invoice total must equal the sum of the printed lines.
Agree with Finance. Per-line rounding, then sum.

Ran a read-only check against the reporting replica (via @Petra Vogel), output below:
invoice lines sum(raw) round(sum) sum(round) diff
INV-2026-0017 2 2.0100 2.01 2.02 -0.01
INV-2025-1184 3 15.0150 15.02 15.03 -0.01
INV-2025-1302 2 4.0050 4.01 4.01 0.00
INV-2026-0231 4 88.0050 88.01 88.02 -0.01
INV-2026-0388 2 0.6700 0.67 0.68 -0.01
INV-2026-0402 5 120.3350 120.34 120.34 0.00
checked 182,406 invoices, 4 differ (all by -0.01), 0 differ by more
query: per-line amount = quantity * unit_price, unrounded; compared Money.Round(sum) with sum(Money.Round(line))
note: differences only appear when two or more lines end in exactly half a cent
note: no invoice is off by more than one cent; stored payments are not affected
note: Bluefen Bakery's payment of 2.02 for INV-2026-0017 is correct; the invoice total is wrong
note: the reminder email for INV-2026-0017 also quoted 2.01, because it uses the same total
runtime: 41.2s on the reporting replica, read-only, no locks taken
next: per-line rounding fix in Invoice.Total, then re-run this check; expected result is 0 invoices differ
owner of the check script: Dana Novak; kept in the #billing-dev channel pins for the next month-end close
Adding a regression case to the QA plan: two lines of 3 × 0.335 must give 2.02.
The UI shows whatever total the API returns. No frontend change needed.
Note for whoever picks this up: do not change Money.Round itself. Single-line rounding is correct.
No operational impact. Ship with the next release train.
AC updated: round each line first, then sum. Ready for development.
